text:
anya: Quick async check — our canary showed mismatched logprob totals between streaming events and the final response when a stop sequence fires before max_tokens. Is the right answer to recompute final logprobs at the end, or should we expose both and leave clients to decide? cc @brent @mike

anya: Example payload we used:
```json
{
  "prompt": "Tell a short story.",
  "stop": ["\n"],
  "max_tokens": 64,
  "stream": true,
  "logprobs": 5
}
```

brent: short answer — streaming events are emitted as tokens are sampled, we don't recompute after stop. So streaming logprobs are "incremental" and can differ from a synchronous final pass that truncates/renormalizes. That's expected behavior today.

mike: to quantify: in the canary we saw streaming cumulative logprob ~ -123.4, final response score (after re-eval) ~ -119.8. The discrepancy came when the stop token cut off mid-beam-normalization for some rare tokens.

sara: my 2c — exposing both seems safest for backward compatibility. Add `final_logprobs` field on non-streaming final event (or an explicit `recomputed_logprobs` flag). Default behavior should stay the same so existing clients relying on streaming events don't break.

anya: proposal: add optional param `recompute_logprobs` (default false) where if true and `stream=true` we buffer and recompute the final token probs and emit an extra final event with `recomputed_logprobs`. That would be opt-in. Thoughts on naming?

brent: naming nit — I'd prefer `logprobs_mode` enum: `stream | final | both`. It gives clearer semantics and avoids combinatorial flags. But runtime cost is higher for `final`/`both`.

mike: technical detail — we can often recompute final logprobs cheaply by re-running the softmax on cached logits (no full sampling), so cost isn't always a full extra forward pass. However for some quantized/optimized kernels we can't always reconstruct logits reliably; there are model/quantization edgecases. We should enumerate which model variants support cheap re-score.

anya: good point. We should add model capability flags in the catalog (e.g., `supports_recompute_logprobs`). Also need to consider burst SLOs — recompute might push some requests over latency SLO.

sara: ops concern — if clients start enabling `final` mode broadly, Dedicated customers might incur extra cost. Let's gate a canary and a rollout plan: enable for 5% hosted traffic, monitor p50/p95, token-cost delta. Also add a feature flag for Dedicated/Private to opt in.

brent: I'm happy to prototype the API contract change. I'll draft a spec PR that adds `logprobs_mode` with default `stream`. It will also document that `final` implies potential recompute cost and may be unsupported on older quantization profiles.

mike: I'll run a quick experiment on a few model variants to see which kernels can return reliable logits for re-score. Will post results in this thread.

deploy-bot: Canary run 2026-03-01T11:20:09Z — id=canary-1789 — observed logprob-discrepancy rate: 0.7% (threshold 0.1%).

anya: thanks all. Brent — can you own the spec PR? Mike — paste kernel/variant results here when ready. I'll file an issue for rollout + docs. Created #1789 (link: https://issues.redwood.ai/1789)

sara: +1 on spec + canary gating. Also we should add a short note in migration docs: "clients that depend on streaming logprobs must continue to work; opt-in `final` mode changes semantics."

anya: perfect — that's a plan. :clap:
